section.title: Introduction and Overview
section.p: lets a module intercept parts of the Wimp's internal processing of and window redraw, by supplying the address of a routine to be called at one of several fixed points. These points are called filter types, and cover the delivery of events, the redraw of window rectangles, the copying of screen blocks, and the rendering of custom icon borders.

The Wimp holds a single registered address for each filter type. Registering a new address for a type that already has one replaces the previous registration; it does not add to a chain. Because of this, only one client at a time can usefully hold a direct registration for a given filter type. FilterManager exists to work around this limit: it is itself the sole direct client of for every filter type it needs, and provides its own registration SWIs (Filter_RegisterPreFilter and related calls) so that any number of tasks can attach a filter of a given type. When FilterManager's own dispatch routine is called by the Wimp, it walks its list of registered filters of that type and calls each of them in turn, using the same calling convention the Wimp itself uses.

This chapter documents the interface itself, and the calling convention for each of the seven filter types - the entry points that FilterManager (or any other direct client of the SWI) must supply to the Wimp, and that FilterManager in turn calls on behalf of each task that has registered a filter with it.

section.title: Technical details
section.p: A registered filter routine is called directly, as a subroutine, from within the Wimp's own processing - it is not entered as a SWI or a vector claim, and there is no error-return convention. Unless stated otherwise for a particular filter type, a filter routine must preserve every register it does not use.

R12 holds the value that was supplied in R2 when the routine was registered with . This is normally a workspace pointer, and is the only value a filter routine can rely on to identify which module or task it belongs to.

Two filter types can signal that they have claimed the call, in different ways. PostFilter returns R0 as -1 to claim an event, but every registered filter is still called regardless of a claim; the event is only reported to the polling task as claimed once every filter has had its turn. IconBorderFilter claims a Draw, Fill, or Colour operation by returning R9 as -1, which stops any further filters being called for that operation - a filter that only augments another filter's rendering, rather than replacing it, must leave R9 unchanged so that later filters still run. Filters of every other type, and the Size and State operations of IconBorderFilter, are purely observational as far as the Wimp is concerned - they cannot prevent the operation they were called about from completing, only act alongside it (for example, by drawing additional screen content, or adjusting an event before it is delivered).

RectFilter, PostRectFilter, PostIconFilter and CopyFilter are all called during window redraw, and are given a window handle rather than a task handle, since redraw is not necessarily driven by the window's owning task. IconBorderFilter filters are registered against a bitmask of border types, given as R3 to when a client of FilterManager registers its filter; only filters whose mask includes the border type being rendered are called.

category.title: Icon border bounding box
category.p: The R2 register of an IconBorderFilter call points to a bounding box block, in screen coordinates:

offset-table.offset: left edge of the icon's bounding box
bottom edge of the icon's bounding box
right edge of the icon's bounding box
top edge of the icon's bounding box
a second border extent in x, whose exact meaning depends on the border style
a second border extent in y, whose exact meaning depends on the border style

category.p: For the size operation, a filter updates x0-y1 in place, insetting the box by the border it is responsible for.

category.title: Icon border colours
category.p: The R3 register of an IconBorderFilter call, for the Draw, Fill, and Colour operations, points to an array of colour words, one for each of the icon's rendering colour roles:
The Colour operation fills in these colours from the window's background colour, given in R4; the Draw and Fill operations use the colours already present.

category.title: Icon border state flags
category.p: The State operation of IconBorderFilter contributes flags into R3 describing how a border style behaves:

bitfield-table.bit: the border's shape can change, so it needs full redraws rather than incremental ones
the border supports a highlighted state
the border does not support a highlighted state

service-definition.name: WimpRegisterFilters
service-definition.description: The Wimp requires its filter handlers to be (re-)installed

entry.register-use: &hex;86 (reason code)

use.p: Broadcast by the Wimp when it starts, or restarts, and needs filter handlers to be installed. A Wimp restart discards any addresses previously given to , so a module holding filter registrations must treat this service as an instruction to re-issue for every filter type it still has filters attached to. Filter types with nothing currently registered do not need to be touched.

swi-definition.name: Wimp_RegisterFilter
swi-definition.description: Registers or removes a filter routine for one aspect of Wimp processing

entry.register-use: Filter type:
address of the routine to call for this filter type, or 0 to remove the current registration for this type
value to place in R12 whenever the routine is called, or 0 when removing a registration

use.p: Sets, replaces, or removes the routine the Wimp calls for one filter type. There is a single registration slot per filter type: registering a new address for a type that already has one silently replaces it, and there is no way to discover what was previously registered. Registering with R1 and R2 both 0 removes the current registration for that type, so that the Wimp no longer calls out for it.
An out-of-range filter type in R0 produces an error.

section.title: Entry points
section.p: Each of the following describes the calling convention a routine must follow to be registered for the given filter type, whether it is registered directly with or, as is normal, attached through FilterManager's own Filter_Register...Filter SWIs and called by FilterManager on the Wimp's behalf.

entry-definition.name: PreFilter
entry-definition.description: Called before the Wimp examines a task's event mask in Wimp_Poll

entry.register-use: the task's event mask, as passed to
task handle of the polling task

exit.register-use: the event mask to use in place of the one supplied

use.p: Called on entry to , before the Wimp uses the event mask to decide which events may wake the task. A filter may change the mask in R0, for example to force the task to be woken for an event it would otherwise have masked out. Where more than one filter of this type is registered against a task, each sees the mask as left by the one before it.
When registered through FilterManager, a filter is only called if it was registered for task 0 (meaning every task) or for the task named in R2.

entry-definition.name: PostFilter
entry-definition.description: Called for each event about to be delivered by Wimp_Poll

entry.register-use: event code, as would be returned by
pointer to the event block
task handle of the polling task

exit.register-use: the event code to deliver instead, or -1 to claim the event
unchanged, or updated to describe a modified event

use.p: Called on exit from , once for every event that is about to be returned to the polling task. A filter may change the event code or the contents of the event block pointed to by R1, or claim the event entirely by returning R0 as -1, in which case the event is not delivered to the task at all.

When more than one filter of this type is registered, every one of them is still called even after one has claimed the event, but each sees the original, unclaimed, event code rather than -1 or another filter's modification; the event is only reported to the task as claimed once every registered filter has had a turn.

A filter is registered against an event mask (a bit per event number, up to event 31; higher event numbers cannot be masked). A set bit means the filter is not interested in that event, matching the sense of the event mask used by itself. A filter is only called for an event it has not masked out, and, when registered through FilterManager, only if it was registered for task 0 or for the task named in R2.

entry-definition.name: CopyFilter
entry-definition.description: Called when the Wimp copies a rectangular block of screen

entry.register-use: destination bounding box, as screen coordinates
source bounding box, as screen coordinates
window handle - 1

use.p: Called whenever the Wimp copies a rectangular area of screen from one place to another, for example while scrolling a window. A filter can use this to keep overlay content, drawn outside the Wimp's own redraw of the window, aligned with the part of the screen that has moved.
Copy filters are not registered against a task, and every registered copy filter is called for every block copy, regardless of which window or task caused it.

entry-definition.name: RectFilter
entry-definition.description: Called before the Wimp redraws the icons in a window rectangle

entry.register-use: task handle of the task that owns the window being redrawn
window handle - 1

use.p: Called once for each rectangle the Wimp is about to redraw within a window, before any of the window's icons in that rectangle have been drawn. A filter can use this to draw content that should sit behind the window's icons.
When registered through FilterManager, a filter is only called if it was registered for task 0 or for the task named in R2.

entry-definition.name: PostRectFilter
entry-definition.description: Called after the Wimp has redrawn the icons in a window rectangle

entry.register-use: task handle of the task that owns the window being redrawn
screen coordinates of the rectangle that was redrawn
window handle - 1

use.p: Called once for each rectangle the Wimp has just finished redrawing within a window, after all of the window's icons in that rectangle have been drawn. A filter can use this to draw content on top of the window's own icons.
When registered through FilterManager, a filter is only called if it was registered for task 0 or for the task named in R2.

entry-definition.name: PostIconFilter
entry-definition.description: Called between rectangles during window redraw, after the previous rectangle's icons

entry.register-use: task handle of the task that owns the window being redrawn
screen coordinates of the rectangle just completed
window handle - 1

use.p: Called during window redraw once the Wimp has finished drawing the icons for one rectangle and is about to move on to the next, or to finish. Unlike PostRectFilter, this is not a per-rectangle "after" call paired with a "before" call - it is a single point between rectangles, used by filters that need to act once the icons for a rectangle are settled without needing to know about the start of the next one.
When registered through FilterManager, a filter is only called if it was registered for task 0 or for the task named in R2.

entry-definition.name: IconBorderFilter
entry-definition.description: Called to draw, size, fill, or colour a custom icon border

entry.register-use: border type
icon flags
pointer to an icon border bounding box block
meaning depends on the operation in R9 - see below
dithering flags, for the Fill and Draw operations; the window's background colour, for the Colour operation; unused otherwise

operation:
draw the border into the box given in R2, using the colours in R3 calculate the border's size, insetting the box in R2 by the border fill the border, within the box given in R2, using the colours in R3 set up the colours in R3 to be used for the border contribute state flags describing how the border behaves, into R3

exit.register-use: unchanged, or -1 to claim the call (Draw, Fill, and Colour operations only - see below)

use.p: Called whenever the Wimp needs to draw, size, fill, or set up colours for an icon whose border type is not one of the Wimp's own built-in styles, or to ask what a border style's rendering needs. A filter is registered against a bitmask of the border types it handles, and is only called for a border type included in that mask.

For the Draw, Fill, and Colour operations, a filter claims the call by returning R9 as -1; no further filter is then called for this request, and the Wimp uses whatever the claiming filter left in the other registers. A filter that only augments another filter's rendering, rather than replacing it, must leave R9 unchanged so that later filters still get their turn.

For the Size operation, a filter updates the box pointed to by R2 in place; this operation is never claimed, so every registered filter for the border type is called and each sees the box as left by the one before it.

For the State operation, a filter contributes its state flags by ORing them into R3, which holds the flags accumulated from any earlier filters (initially clear); this operation is never claimed either, so every registered filter for the border type is called.

section.title: Examples
section.p: Registering a PreFilter routine directly with the Wimp:

p.extended-example: ADR R1, my_pre_filter MOV R2, R12 ; workspace pointer MOV R0, #0 ; 0 = PreFilter SWI "Wimp_RegisterFilter"
MOV R0, #0 ; 0 = PreFilter MOV R1, #0 MOV R2, #0 SWI "Wimp_RegisterFilter"

revision.title: Corrected IconBorderFilter
revision.change: Corrected IconBorderFilter: it does have a claim protocol (R9 = -1 stops further filters being called for the Draw, Fill, and Colour operations), contrary to the previous revision. Added the icon border bounding box and colour array structures, and resolved the State operation's register layout, which had previously been marked unconfirmed.
Added the icon border state flags bitfield table (WimpFilterIBS_ChangesShape and WimpFilterIBS_Highlightable), rather than only naming the flags in prose.
